page: Google Cloud Platform m3-megamem-64 is a memory-optimized server instance designed for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. It features 64 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.6 GHz, with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 976.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 15.25 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes.

Benchmark results show strong multi-threaded performance, particularly in memory-bound and compute-heavy tasks. The instance achieved a strong Geekbench multi-core score of 16654.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 54571.25. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached a strong 293.92 GB/sec. In database operations, the server demonstrated strong performance with a PassMark database score of 26047.32, while Redis SET operations maintained an average of 53.57 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth tests recorded 150.66 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 62.1 GB/sec for large block write operations.

The Intel Xeon processor includes hardware-level support for AVX, AVX-512, and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI, though it lacks AMX matrix extensions. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m3-megamem-64 offers high memory density per vCPU, making it a specialized option for workloads where RAM capacity is the primary bottleneck rather than raw single-core CPU speed. This profile is highly suited for large in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning systems, heavy data analytics, and memory-intensive ETL pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform m3-megamem-64 is an x86_64 memory-optimized server instance configured with 64 vCPUs and 976.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 15.25 GB per vCPU. Powered by a 2.6 GHz Intel Xeon processor with 32 physical cores and a 54 MB L3 cache, this instance features dedicated CPU allocation and supports AVX-512 and cryptographic instructions. It does not include local storage or GPUs. Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities in multi-threaded operations, with a PassMark CPU score of 54571.25 and strong database operation metrics. Conversely, single-core performance and memory bandwidth remain in the average tier. This hardware profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound enterprise applications, making it highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, data analytics, and complex ETL processing where massive memory capacity is required.
